summary: Jean-François Jarrige was an archaeology and Indology scholar who earned his doctorate from the University of Paris and studied at École du Louvre and Lycée Claude Fauriel. He served as director (1986–2004) and president (~1986–2008) of the Musée Guimet.

Jean-François Lyotard was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, University of Paris, and Paris Nanterre University. His teaching career included posts at Paris 8 University (1972–1987), UC Irvine (~1987–1998), and Emory University (~1993–1998).
Jean-François Revel was a scholar in the field of philosophy. He completed his education at Lycée Jean-Baptiste-Say, lycée du Parc (~1941–1943), and the École Normale Supérieure (1943).

Jean-Louis Burnouf worked in linguistics and related fields, studying under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He held chairs at Lycée Louis-le-Grand (~1808–1826) and the Collège de France (1816–1844), later serving as university librarian at Sorbonne University (1840).
Jean-Luc Achard is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and held a post at the CNRS.

Jean-Luc Chevillard is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at École Normale Supérieure and under Antoine Culioli. He has held positions as a CNRS researcher (attested 2009) and Lehrbeauftragter at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Jean-Noël Robert is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who studied under Bernard Frank and at INALCO. He held posts at the CNRS (1975–1990), EPHE (from 1979), and served as director at Collège de France (2010–2022).

Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat was a scholar of sinology and linguistics who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy and at INALCO. He held the Chair of Sinology at the Collège de France (1814–1832) and co-founded the Société Asiatique in 1822.

Jean-Pierre Drège is a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Yves Hervouet at the University of Burgundy and INALCO. He served as president of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1998–2004).

Jeannine Auboyer specialized in Indology and archaeology, studying at École du Louvre, EPHE, Sorbonne, and under scholars including René Grousset. She served as chief curator at Musée Guimet (1965–1980) and held a chair at École du Louvre (1965–1980).

Jeff Dolven studied at the University of Oxford and Yale University, where he earned a PhD in English. His academic appointments include a junior fellowship at Harvard and a professorship in English at Princeton University (~2002).

Jeff Malpas is a philosopher who studied at the University of Auckland and Australian National University (PhD). He led Murdoch University's philosophy programme (~1990–1999) and served as Professor (1999) and Emeritus Distinguished Professor (2018) at the University of Tasmania.

Jeff Ralph works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a religious studies degree at Queen's University at Kingston and earned his doctorate at the University of Victoria under supervisor Duncan M. Taylor.
Jeff Shore is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He held an academic post at Hanazono University as Professor (~1987–2023) and subsequently became professor emeritus (~2023).
Jeff Watt is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. He studied under Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima and held a post at the Rubin Museum of Art.

Jeff Wilson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, having studied under mentor Taitetsu Unno and postdoctoral mentor Myōsei Tatsuguchi.

Jeffery D. Long is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned a BA from Notre Dame and an MA and PhD from the University of Chicago. In 2000, he became Associate Professor at Elizabethtown College.

Jeffrey Broughton is a scholar in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD from Columbia University (1975) and served as a professor in the Department of Religious Studies at California State University (attested 2004).

Jeffrey Clark Ruff is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Missouri State University and UC Santa Barbara under David Gordon White. He served at UCSB, the University of California, and joined Marshall University in 2002.

Jeffrey Davis Schoening is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Washington (attested 1991), where he studied under Collett Cox and Sanghasen Singh.
